epithet: What stays, and what is carried off
lede: Rain falls; each valley fills to its own measure; the flood comes down carrying a crest of foam. The foam is thrown aside and gone. What is of use to people stays in the ground. That, says this surah, is truth and falsehood — and it says it under a sky in which the thunder itself is glorifying Allah.

names.name: al-Raʿd
names.note: From its thirteenth ayah: “The thunder glorifies Him with His praise, and so do the angels, in awe of Him.”

revelation.detail: Ibn al-Jawzī sets out two sayings, each with a report from Ibn ʿAbbās behind it. That it is Makkan: related from him by ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭalḥah, and held by al-Ḥasan, Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, ʿAṭāʾ and Qatādah. That it is Madinan: related from him by ʿAṭāʾ al-Khurāsānī, and held by Jābir ibn Zayd. Each side then excepts a few ayat for the other. Al-Qurṭubī reports the same division; Ibn Kathīr heads it Makkan, and its subjects — the oneness of Allah, the resurrection, the truth of the message — are those of the Makkan surahs. The muṣḥaf heads it Madinan, and the traditional order places it ninety-sixth.
revelation.when: Makkah, on one saying from Ibn ʿAbbās; Madinah, on the other

evidence.quote: اخْتَلَفُوا في نُزُولِها عَلى قَوْلَيْنِ: أحَدُهُما: أنَّها مَكِّيَّةٌ، رَواهُ عَلِيُّ بْنُ أبِي طَلْحَةَ عَنِ ابْنِ عَبّاسٍ، وبِهِ قالَ الحَسَنُ، وسَعِيدُ بْنُ جُبَيْرٍ، وعَطاءٌ، وقَتادَةُ
والثّانِي: أنَّها مَدَنِيَّةٌ، رَواهُ عَطاءٌ الخُراسانِيُّ عَنِ ابْنِ عَبّاسٍ، وبِهِ قالَ جابِرُ ابْنُ زَيْدٍ
سُورَةُ الرَّعْدِ مَكِّيَّةٌ فِي قَوْلِ الْحَسَنِ وَعِكْرِمَةَ وَعَطَاءٍ وَجَابِرٍ، وَمَدَنِيَّةٌ فِي قَوْلِ الْكَلْبِيِّ وَمُقَاتِلٍ

setting: Its first ayah states the difficulty the whole surah addresses: “What has been sent down to you from your Lord is the truth; but most people do not believe.” If it is the truth, why is it not winning? Why do those who deny it prosper, and demand a sign, and go unpunished? The surah answers by changing where the listener is looking.

It looks up. “Allah is He who raised the heavens without pillars that you can see, then rose over the Throne, and pressed the sun and the moon into service, each running to an appointed term.” It looks down: “In the earth are neighbouring tracts, and gardens of vines, and crops, and palms in clusters and alone — watered with one water; yet We make some better than others to eat.” It looks inward: “Allah knows what every female carries, and by how much the wombs fall short or exceed. Everything with Him is by measure.” Each person has angels in succession, before him and behind him, guarding him by Allah’s command.

Then the storm. “He it is who shows you the lightning, for fear and for hope, and raises the heavy clouds. The thunder glorifies Him with His praise, and so do the angels, in awe of Him.” Ibn al-Jawzī records that most held the next words — “He sends the thunderbolts and strikes with them whom He wills, while they dispute about Allah” — to have come down about two men who came to the Prophet ﷺ meaning to kill him, one of whom was burned by a bolt out of a clear summer sky.

And out of the storm, the surah’s great image. The water comes down and the valleys flow, each according to its measure, and the torrent carries a swelling foam; and from the ore that men heat in the fire for ornaments and tools there rises a scum like it. “Thus Allah sets out truth and falsehood. As for the foam, it passes away as dross; and as for what benefits people, it remains in the earth.” Falsehood is loud, and on top, and soon gone. That is the answer to the first ayah.

For those who hold to the truth while it is still under the surface, the surah has the gentlest line it could give: “Those who believe, and whose hearts find rest in the remembrance of Allah. Truly, in the remembrance of Allah do hearts find rest.”

occasions.title: The thunderbolt
occasions.text: Arbad ibn Qays and ʿĀmir ibn al-Ṭufayl came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ meaning to kill him. He said: “O Allah, suffice me against them by what You will.” As for Arbad, Allah sent a thunderbolt upon him on a clear summer’s day, and it burned him; and ʿĀmir was struck by a tumour and died. Then Allah sent down this ayah. Ibn al-Jawzī gives this as the saying of the majority, and two others beside it.
occasions.source: Ibn al-Jawzī, from Ibn Jurayj and others — a report of the commentators, not one of the Ṣaḥīḥ collections.

evidence.quote: أرْبَدَ بْنِ قَيْسٍ، وعامِرِ بْنِ الطُّفَيْلِ، أتَيا إلى رَسُولِ اللَّهِ ﷺ يُرِيدانِ الفَتْكَ بِهِ، فَقالَ: " اللَّهُمَّ اكْفِنِيهِما بِما شِئْتَ "، فَأمّا أرْبَدُ فَأرْسَلَ اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ صاعِقَةً في يَوْمٍ صائِفٍ صاحٍ فَأحْرَقَتْهُ

aim: To show what power truly is — the power of Allah, and where it is seen — and to affirm the promise and the threat, and Allah’s way in changing and replacing.
themes: Signs in the sky and the soil
Truth and falsehood: the foam and the ore

outline.title: The truth, and the signs
outline.summary: Alif Lām Mīm Rā. These are the ayat of the Book; and what has been sent down to you from your Lord is the truth, but most people do not believe. Allah is He who raised the heavens without pillars that you can see. He spread out the earth, and set in it firm mountains and rivers. In the earth are neighbouring tracts, watered with one water. If you wonder — then wondrous is their saying: “When we are dust, shall we be in a new creation?” They say: “Why has no sign been sent down to him?” You are only a warner; and for every people there is a guide.

outline.title: Knowledge, thunder, and the parable
outline.summary: Allah knows what every female carries. For each there are angels in succession, before and behind him. Allah does not change what is in a people until they change what is in themselves. He shows you the lightning, for fear and hope; the thunder glorifies Him with His praise. To Him is the true call. To Allah prostrates whoever is in the heavens and the earth, willingly or unwillingly, and their shadows too. He sends down water from the sky, and the valleys flow by their measure, and the torrent carries a rising foam. As for the foam, it passes away as dross; and what benefits people remains in the earth (13:17).

outline.title: The people of understanding
outline.summary: Is one who knows that what has been sent down to you is the truth like one who is blind? Those who fulfil the covenant of Allah; who join what Allah has commanded to be joined; who are patient, seeking the Face of their Lord; who keep up the prayer, spend secretly and openly, and repel evil with good — theirs is the final home: gardens of Eden, and the angels entering upon them from every gate: “Peace be upon you, for what you patiently bore.” Those who believe, and whose hearts find rest in the remembrance of Allah.

outline.title: A Qurʾan that would move mountains
outline.summary: Thus We have sent you among a community before which others have passed, while they disbelieve in the Most Merciful. Were there a Qurʾan by which mountains could be moved, or the earth cleft, or the dead made to speak — the whole matter belongs to Allah. Messengers were mocked before you. Is He who stands over every soul, watching what it has earned, like any other? The likeness of the Garden promised to the mindful: rivers flow beneath it; its fruit is everlasting, and its shade.

outline.title: The Mother of the Book
outline.summary: We sent messengers before you, and gave them wives and offspring. For every term there is a decree. Allah erases what He wills and confirms, and with Him is the Mother of the Book. Whether We show you part of what We promise them or take you first, upon you is only the conveying. Do they not see that We come to the land, reducing it from its borders? Those who disbelieve say: “You are not a messenger.” Say: “Allah is enough as a witness between me and you.”

keyAyah.why: Its answer for the believer who must wait while falsehood is still on the surface: where the heart can rest in the meantime.

virtues.text: The Jews came to the Prophet ﷺ and said: “Abū l-Qāsim, tell us about the thunder: what is it?” He said: “One of the angels, put in charge of the clouds; with him are rods of fire with which he drives the clouds where Allah wills.” They said: “And this sound that we hear?” He said: “His driving of the clouds, when he urges them on, until they reach where he has been commanded.” They said: “You have spoken the truth.”

“The keys of the unseen are five, which none knows but Allah: none knows what tomorrow holds but Allah; none knows what the wombs fall short of but Allah; none knows when the rain will come but Allah; no soul knows in what land it will die; and none knows when the Hour will arise but Allah.”

virtuesNote: The fifteenth ayah is an ayah of prostration. It is related from ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Zubayr, in Mālik’s Muwaṭṭaʾ, that when he heard thunder he would stop speaking and say: “Glory be to Him whom the thunder glorifies with His praise, and the angels, in awe of Him.”
before: Yūsuf ended: “How many a sign in the heavens and the earth do they pass by, turning away from it.” Al-Raʿd names those signs one by one.
after: Al-Raʿd closes with the disbelievers saying, “You are not a messenger.” Sūrat Ibrāhīm opens with what the Messenger was sent to do: bring mankind out of darknesses into the light.
